label: Sat 21 Nov 2026
headline: Today's sound headlines
lead: 30 new stories from 15 sound and audio news sources over the last 48 hours, including Sound On Sound, Production Expert, ProSoundWeb, FOH, TPi and 10 more. This edition is assembled automatically from the outlets' own feeds: titles and summaries are theirs, sorted into sections. Open a story for the full article.

items.title: 7 Free Plugins From Lydtrold That Support AAX DSP
items.take: Lydtrold has a free collection of 16 plug-ins, and all of them support AAX Native. Seven also support AAX DSP, which is good news for Pro Tools users with HDX cards and for Avid Carbon users.

items.take: Kami brings together compression and subtle saturation, and is said to combine the immediacy of a compressor pedal with the flexibility of a fully fledged studio tool.

items.title: Signal To Noise, Episode 337: Sound Designer Luke Swaffield On Immersive Audio & More

items.title: Never Found Audio releases VF-Mini, a FREE reverse riser plugin for vocals
items.take: The latest release from the developer Never Found Audio is the VF-Mini, a free reverse riser plugin for vocals. Like Never Found Audio’s previous Mini series FX plugins, VF-Mini is the free version of a paid product: VF-Pro.

items.take: Whitaker received the David Sarnoff Medal, while Clarke was inducted as a SMPTE Fellow

items.title: Nine Inch Nails fans can now stream nearly 2000 live recordings
items.take: NIN fans, it's a momentous week. For nearly 20 years, the Nine Inch Nails archive has been compiling live shows from 1988 to today; that's now nearly 2000 recordings of over 1200 concerts. The site is a pleasure to navigate now, and this week came big news: streaming, on demand.

items.title: The Shape of Dread – Different Forms a Suspense Curve Can Take
items.take: Every tense scene you’ve ever sat through, eyes wide-open, phone forgotten in your hand, works because someone carefully constructed it. And one of the tools a filmmaker has at hand is the so-called suspense curve. It’s not a storyboard, not a shot list, not a carefully crafted previs.

craft.body:
New hardware usually forces a new operating system, and audio software is always the last to catch up. Treat your working machine like a show system: no OS updates in the middle of a project, and no new computer for a paid session until you have run a full session on it.

Keep a one-page list of every driver, plugin, licence manager and control-surface app you depend on, and check it against each vendor's compatibility page before any upgrade. Keep the old machine set up until the new one has finished a real job. Clients never see the upgrade, only the session that wouldn't open.
craft.title: Freeze your OS during a job
